newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebed honours French wartime leader de Gaulle.
newsitem.headline: Lebed honours French wartime leader de Gaulle.

text.p: COLOMBEY-LES-DEUX-EGLISES, France, Feb 18 - Russian presidential hopeful Alexander Lebed paid homage to General Charles de Gaulle on Tuesday with a symbolic pilgrimage to the French wartime leader's final resting place.
Lebed, Russia's security chief until his sacking by President Boris Yeltsin in October, worked in the visit to the tomb of one of his personal heroes during a five-day private visit to France.
In a clear sign of his admiration for forceful French military leaders, Lebed had also hoped to visit Napoleon's tomb in Paris but was forced to cancel those plans due to a painful in-grown toenail.
He also planned talks with Philippe de Gaulle, the late head of state's son and a member of the French Senate.
There are obvious parallels between de Gaulle and Lebed, who at age 46 is considered the front-runner to succeed Yeltsin should Russia hold new presidential elections.

De Gaulle led a dispirited France out of the World War Two era and later ended France's war in Algeria while Lebed ended a Russian war in rebel Chechnya and hopes to lead a dispirited Russia out of a period of tough economic and political challenges should he one day win the presidency.

"This burden is very heavy, but I will lift it," Lebed remarked somewhat cryptically to reporters during his visit to the village of Colombey-les-Deux Eglises. "You can make a mark on history, and you can end up burning your wings."
Lebed flew by helicopter from Paris to the village where de Gaulle lived and died.

Despite strong winds and a steady drizzle, he took in all of the village's principal tourist sites, laying a wreath at the de Gaulle monument, visiting de Gaulle's residence and touring the village cemetery before signing the visitors' book and heading back to Paris.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said France was aware of Lebed's potential role at home. "Mr Lebed certainly has a role to play in Russia today and tomorrow," he told RTL radio.
The Foreign Ministry said on Monday that Lebed was due to meet a senior ministry official this week. But no contacts with government members are planned.
Lebed was scheduled to meet Senate speaker Rene Monory and business leaders as well as de Gaulle on Tuesday.
In an interview on French television Arte aired on Monday, Lebed said he would encourage business investment in Russia through common-sense economic policies.

"Investments are not being made...because there are no rules of the game, whether domestically or in Russia's international relations," he said. "I want to put rules of the game in place. I want good sense to triumph."
In response to a question, he said friends and former military colleagues who are now heads of small and medium-sized businesses and who support his ideas were paying for his visit to France.
